Name: reconstruction_pays_only_across_the_writer_gap
Title: Reconstruction Pays Only Across the Writer Gap: Reader-Side Rewriting of Foreign Experience Helps by Policy Distance, Not Writer Capability, at Matched Tokens
Short Hypothesis: Training-free read-time reconstruction (the reader rewrites the retrieved items into a plan in its own action format, conditioned on its current observation) adds nothing over verbatim injection when the writer is the reader itself, and adds a gain that grows with writer-reader policy distance (same backbone under a different scaffold/temperature; a different 32B backbone) but not with writer capability (same backbone in thinking mode), when the comparison is made against verbatim injection at matched consumer tokens (k=7) and net of a reconstruction placebo applied to the static procedure prompt.
Related Work: MemHarness (2607.28272) shows critique-and-reconstruct beats verbatim replay, but the retrieved experience is the agent's own, the reconstruction policy is GRPO-trained (so the gain is not separated from training), and per-step token cost is not matched. Echo (2604.05533) adapts the agent's own Minecraft experience analogically; 2406.14596 abstracts sub-optimal demonstrations with human feedback; neither varies the writer. AdaCoM (2605.30785) finds that how much a frozen agent's context should be compressed depends on the agent's own baseline strength, but manages the agent's own trajectory, not another writer's experience, and reports no writer x reader cell. The cross-embodiment imitation literature (ImMimic 2509.10952, TrajSkill 2510.07773) translates demonstrations across a domain gap, which is the mechanism claimed here, but has no LLM-text analogue with the demonstrator manipulated at matched cost. Measurement A on this node gives the verbatim expert->Qwen3-32B baseline (+27/+32 net at k=3, k=7 no harm, look-at-in-light -4.8); nothing on this node has measured any adaptation step. Archived closer_beats_stronger (5.75) claimed proximity predicts raw transfer without separating it from capability and without a self-pool control; archived abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) varies abstraction level within one writer and holds the writer fixed.
Abstract: Adaptation methods for agent memory (reconstruction, analogical adaptation, abstraction) are validated only on experience the agent wrote itself, so it is unknown whether the adaptation step is a planning aid that helps regardless of who wrote the item, or a translation step whose value depends on the writer. We manipulate the writer of an ALFWorld experience bank while holding the task set, bank construction, retriever and reader fixed: expert walkthroughs, the reader's own successes, the same backbone under a different scaffold and temperature (policy distance at fixed capability), the same backbone in thinking mode (capability at fixed backbone), and a second 32B backbone's successes; two readers (Qwen3-32B, EXAONE-4.0-32B) read every bank. For each writer x reader cell we compare verbatim injection at k=3 and k=7 against training-free reconstruction at k=3 (the reader rewrites the three items into one plan in its own action format conditioned on the first observation; the plan replaces the items), and against a reconstruction placebo (the same rewriting prompt applied to the static six-procedure prompt and to items retrieved for the wrong task type, token-matched). The estimands are the retained-gain ratio per cell before and after reconstruction and the reconstruction increment over token-matched verbatim injection, net of the placebo, with cluster-bootstrap CIs over 274 games x 4 seeds for the headline cells. The central claim is an interaction: the increment is near zero for the self-written bank and largest for the distant banks, ordered by policy distance rather than by writer capability. A null interaction, or an increment that is largest for the reader's own bank, falsifies it; the self-pool cell at matched collection cost and the placebo cells can produce both outcomes. Consumer-side tokens and episodes per minute are reported with every gain.
Experiments:
- Banks (all from the 3,553 train games or the 1,465 expert walkthroughs; success-filtered; type-balanced to the expert pool's type distribution and length-capped at 2x the expert median steps so the writer manipulation is not a length manipulation; the uncapped variant is an ablation): W_exp expert; W_self Qwen3-32B standard ReAct T=0 (on disk); W_prox Qwen3-32B same mode, plan-then-act scaffold with different action phrasing, T=0.7 (collect, ~3 GPU-h; verify k=0 success within +/-5 net of W_self, else lower T); W_cap Qwen3-32B thinking mode, standard scaffold (collect; verify k=0 success differs from W_self by >= 8 net); W_other EXAONE-4.0-32B standard scaffold (collect after serving verification, ~3 GPU-h); W_big gpt-oss-120b only if it serves on one A100.
- Readers: R1 Qwen3-32B standard non-thinking; R2 EXAONE-4.0-32B. Same retriever as Measurement A, k=3 primary. Every bank is read by both readers.
- Conditions per (writer, reader): C0 no memory; C_static the Measurement-C six-procedure prompt; C_v3 verbatim k=3; C_v7 verbatim k=7 (token-matched to reconstruction, ~1,010 injected tokens); C_r3 reconstruction k=3 (one rewrite at step 0 into the reader's action format; a re-reconstruct-every-5-steps variant is an ablation); C_pl_static the reconstruction prompt applied to C_static text (memory-absent placebo); C_pl_mis the reconstruction prompt applied to k=3 items retrieved for a different task type (mismatched placebo, token-matched).
- Estimands: verbatim retained-gain ratio rho_v(w,r) = [S(r,C_v3,w) - S(r,C_static)] / [S(w,C_v3,w) - S(w,C_static)] where the writer policy reads its own bank; rho_r(w,r) with C_r3 in the numerator; reconstruction increment D(w,r) = S(r,C_r3,w) - S(r,C_v7,w), and net increment D*(w,r) = D(w,r) - [S(r,C_pl_static) - S(r,C_static)]; per-type breakdown for the six procedures; consumer tokens per episode (prompt + generated) and episodes/min per cell.
- Gate 0 (before any confirmatory cell): at least one foreign bank yields a verbatim gain net of static >= +10 for R1 at k=3; reconstruction on W_exp does not lower success by more than 4 net (safety). Pre-registered margins are fractions of this Gate-0 verbatim gain.
- Headline cells at 274 games x 4 seeds: (W_self,R1), (W_prox,R1), (W_cap,R1), (W_other,R1) under C_v7 and C_r3, plus the two placebos for R1; all other cells at 274 x 2 seeds. Total ~40 cells, ~24k episodes plus three bank collections; both A100s busy (one serves the reader, the other collects the next bank or serves the second reader); about 2.5 days.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Cheapest baseline first: C_static (Measurement C) and the reconstruction placebo on C_static, both before any retrieval cell.
- Direct injection of the unmodified items at matched tokens (C_v7) is the primary comparator for every reconstruction cell; C_v3 is reported as the cheaper comparator.
- Self-pool control at matched collection cost: W_self for R1 and W_other for R2 are collected at the same episode budget as the foreign banks; every foreign-bank gain is reported against that cell.
- Ablations: length-uncapped banks (does the increment track item wandering rather than writer identity); reconstruct-every-5-steps (does state-conditioning beyond step 0 add anything at its token cost); reconstruction with the writer identity revealed vs hidden in the prompt (does the reader use provenance).
- Named reimplementation: MemHarness-style reconstruction prompt without RL (2607.28272) as C_r3; the GRPO-trained version is out of budget and is named as the untested arm.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (headline interaction): D*(W_other,R1) - D*(W_self,R1) >= 1/3 of the Gate-0 verbatim gain with a 95% cluster-bootstrap CI excluding 0. Falsifier: the difference's CI includes 0 or is negative, i.e. reconstruction helps the reader's own bank as much as or more than the foreign bank. Arm: the (W_self,R1,C_r3/C_v7) cells versus the (W_other,R1,C_r3/C_v7) cells at 4 seeds; the self-bank cell can produce a large increment because self-written successes are wandering on-policy trajectories that rewriting could compress.
- P2 (proximity, not capability): D*(W_prox,R1) - D*(W_self,R1) >= 1/3 of the Gate-0 gain, while D*(W_cap,R1) - D*(W_self,R1) < that margin. Falsifier: the thinking-mode bank shows the larger increment (capability distance governs) or the different-scaffold bank shows none (format distance does not matter). Arms: the (W_prox,R1) and (W_cap,R1) reconstruction and verbatim cells.
- P3 (token-matched): for W_other->R1 and W_exp->R2, S(C_r3) > S(C_v7) by >= 4 net. Falsifier: C_v7 >= C_r3 in either cell (more verbatim items at equal tokens do as well as rewriting). Arm: the C_v7 cells, which Measurement A shows are not harmed relative to k=3.
- P4 (placebo): the memory-absent placebo increment S(C_pl_static) - S(C_static) is < 1/3 of D(W_other,R1). Falsifier: the placebo captures >= 2/3 of the increment (the gain is a planning step, not adaptation of the foreign item). Arm: C_pl_static and C_pl_mis for R1.
- P5 (symmetry across the store): the same W_self bank read by R2 shows rho_r(W_self,R2) - rho_v(W_self,R2) >= 0.15. Falsifier: rho_r <= rho_v for R2 (rewriting does not help the other backbone read Qwen3's experience). Arm: the (W_self,R2) C_v3 and C_r3 cells.
- P6 (where verbatim is negative): reconstruction of W_exp lifts look-at-in-light for R1 from -4.8 to >= 0 net. Falsifier: look-at-in-light stays <= -4.8 under C_r3. Arm: the per-type breakdown of (W_exp,R1,C_r3); secondary because the type cell has ~45 games.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired per-game success differences with games x seeds; cluster bootstrap over games (2,000 resamples, seeds nested) for every estimand and for the interaction contrasts; 274 x 2 seeds for screening cells (+/-8 net) and 274 x 4 seeds for the four headline cells and their placebos (+/-5.7 net; an interaction of two paired differences needs the doubled seed count). One pre-registered headline contrast (P1); P2-P6 are secondary; per-type breakdowns exploratory. Margins are pre-registered as fractions of the measured Gate-0 verbatim gain, not fixed numbers. Consumer-side tokens (prompt and generated, including the reconstruction output) and episodes/min are logged per episode and reported per cell; seeds fix the environment split and sampling; temperature 0 for readers except where the manipulation requires otherwise. Bank collections use nohup runners with append-only JSONL and pid files, workers tuned to the vLLM running queue (>= 8 per replica).
Preprint Collision Check: All queries ran through tools/ideate2/s2cli.py (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, channel s2=ok hf=ok unless noted). (1) recent: 'reconstruct retrieved experience conditioned on current state agent cross-model transfer' -> MemHarness 2607.28272, 2608.26730 (conditional reuse of update evidence in post-training), 2607.13884 Experience Memory Graph, 2606.00547, Echo 2604.05533; none manipulates the writer of the retrieved experience or matches tokens. (2) closest named method: 'MemHarness critique and reconstruct retrieved experience negative transfer verbatim replay' -> 2607.28272, 2604.27003 (memory design trades transfer against forgetting at the retrieval level), otherwise continual-learning replay papers; no writer x reader cell. (3) home: 'cross-domain imitation learning demonstration translation embodiment mismatch' -> ImMimic 2509.10952, TrajSkill 2510.07773, UniSkill 2505.08787, H2R-Bench 2608.13049: demonstration translation across a domain gap is an established mechanism in robotics; no text-experience analogue, no demonstrator manipulation at matched cost. (4) recent: 'context augmentation model execution feedback transfer to different execution agent backbone' -> AdaCoM 2605.30785 (verified with s2cli paper: compression level should depend on the agent's own baseline strength, agent's own context only), CLEAR 2604.07487, HarnessDev 2609.01437 (self-built harnesses transfer poorly across models). Nearest pre-emption is AdaCoM's reader-strength dependence; it does not vary the writer and does not compare against verbatim injection at matched tokens. No result found that reports the adaptation increment as a function of writer identity.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Ceiling: verbatim expert items already give 0.81/0.87 at k=3, so the expert cell has little headroom; the headline therefore rests on W_other, W_prox and W_self, where verbatim gains are expected to be smaller, and Gate 0 requires one of them to clear +10. If EXAONE-4.0-32B does not serve in vLLM 0.13, W_prox and W_cap still give the proximity-vs-capability contrast within one backbone and W_other is dropped (the cross-backbone claim is then unsupported). Reconstruction adds generated tokens and latency (~12-15 episodes/min per replica vs ~20); if the increment is positive but per-token efficiency is below C_v7's, the practical recommendation reverses and is reported as such. The length cap changes the banks; both capped and uncapped results are reported. ALFWorld procedures are few, so 'policy distance' here is mostly scaffold and phrasing distance; a WebShop replication is out of budget.
Addresses gap: G16 (adaptation validated only on self-written experience) as the primary target; G20 (adaptation cost never matched against plain retrieval) through the token-matched C_v7 comparator and the per-cell token and throughput reporting; G18 partially through the retained-gain ratio before and after reconstruction.
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet: Measurement A (expert->Qwen3-32B verbatim, +27/+32 net at k=3, k=7 no harm, look-at-in-light -4.8) measures verbatim injection only; this idea claims the increment of a reconstruction step over that verbatim result and that the increment depends on who wrote the item, which A cannot show because it has one writer and no adaptation arm. Digest card: 2607.28272 MemHarness claims reconstruction beats replay for the agent's own experience with a GRPO-trained policy; this idea claims that training-free reconstruction adds nothing for self-written items and gains only across a writer gap at matched tokens and net of a planning placebo, a claim MemHarness never tests because its writer is always the reader. Archived: abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs varies abstraction within one writer at fixed reader; here abstraction is fixed (raw items) and the writer is the manipulated variable with proximity and capability separated, which closer_beats_stronger did not do.

Name: reconstruction_launders_planted_procedure_errors
Title: Rewriting Launders What It Should Filter: Read-Time Reconstruction Propagates Planted Procedure Errors and Hides Them, While an Explicit Read-Time Gate Detects Foreign Errors Better Than the Reader's Own
Short Hypothesis: When benign-looking wrong items (procedure swaps, relabelled failures, receptacle swaps) are planted at controlled rates in an ALFWorld bank, reader-side reconstruction keeps most of the planted wrong step in its rewritten plan and makes the error harder for a downstream critic to detect than the original item (laundering), whereas an explicit keep/discard gate before use recovers at least half of the harm; and the gate's recall is lower on contaminated items written in the reader's own style than on the same contamination in another 32B backbone's style, for both readers, so the blind spot is a property of writer-reader proximity rather than of any one bank.
Related Work: MemoryGraft (2512.16962) shows benign-looking planted successes drift an agent persistently but evaluates one backbone and no reader-side defense. SkillJack (2608.03509) shows poisoned histories become persistent skills through the agent's own learning pipeline, the closest observation to laundering, but with no rewriting arm, no writer identity and no detector scored by precision and recall. 2605.22842 defines trust laundering across sessions and defends with provenance-aware information-flow control, costed only on adversarial policy documents. MaliciousSkillBench (2608.19901) finds skill detectors generalize poorly across sources with high false positives, but scores externally authored skills, not experience items in the reader's own style. In the home literature, paraphrasing evades AI-text detectors while retrieval defends (2303.13408) and SONAR (2605.01078) sanitizes malicious instructions in RAG with NLI pruning; label-noise work finds wrong labels barely hurt in-context classification (2202.12837), which is why Gate 0 here is a real test rather than an assumption. 2605.29463 shows self-generated reflections store confident wrong interpretations; the own-style blind spot predicted here is its read-time counterpart. Archived lineage_blast_radius was judged entailed by its consolidation rule; here whether a rewrite keeps or fixes a wrong step is an empirical persistence rate, not a rule.
Abstract: Adaptation of foreign experience is assumed to be beneficial, but an adaptation step can also carry a writer's errors into the reader and, by rewriting them in the reader's own words, make them harder to detect. We manufacture contamination in ALFWorld banks written by three writers (expert walkthroughs, Qwen3-32B's own successes, EXAONE-4.0-32B's own successes) with the same operations applied to each: appliance swaps that turn a clean or cool trajectory into a fluent wrong-procedure trajectory, the writer's own failures relabelled as successes, and wrong-but-plausible final receptacles, at 0/10/25/50% of the affected types with item-level labels retained. Two readers read every bank under verbatim injection, reconstruction (rewrite into a plan, no judgment), an explicit read-time gate (keep/discard each item with a reason, then act on the kept items verbatim), gate-then-reconstruct, and a non-LLM keyword rule that checks appliance against task type. Gate 0 requires the harm under verbatim injection to reach 6 net points at some rate. The estimands are harm by rate and writer, the retained-gain ratio in the clean cells, the wrong-step persistence rate in reconstructed plans, downstream critic recall on reconstructed versus original items, and gate precision and recall per writer x reader x operation. The central claims are that reconstruction launders (persistence >= 0.5, critic recall drops) and that detection recall is lowest on the diagonal of the writer x reader matrix, which a 2x2 with both 32B pools read by both readers can separate from a pool property.
Experiments:
- Banks: W_exp, W_self (Qwen3-32B), W_other (EXAONE-4.0-32B, collected after serving verification); W_self and W_other type-balanced and length-matched to each other so the diagonal contrast is not a length contrast. Contamination operations applied identically to each bank: Op-A appliance swap (heat<->cool, clean->heat, bindings preserved; the item reads as a successful trajectory); Op-B relabelled failures (Qwen3: from its 1,661 failed train games; EXAONE: from its failures; expert: walkthroughs truncated before the goal step and annotated as complete); Op-C wrong final receptacle. Rates 0/10/25/50% of the affected types' items; planted items carry hidden labels for scoring.
- Readers R1 Qwen3-32B, R2 EXAONE-4.0-32B; same retriever, k=3. Conditions: C0; C_static (Measurement C six-procedure prompt); C_v3 verbatim; C_r3 reconstruct (as in the companion design, one rewrite at step 0); C_g3 gate (per item keep/discard with a one-sentence reason, kept items injected verbatim, no refill); C_gr3 gate then reconstruct; C_rule keyword rule (appliance token vs task-type keyword) then verbatim; a post-hoc critic (the reader prompted to judge correctness of a plan given its task) applied offline to original planted items and to the C_r3 rewritten plans.
- Estimands: harm H(w,r,op,rate,cond) = S(r,cond,w,0%) - S(r,cond,w,rate); recovery = 1 - H(cond)/H(C_v3); wrong-step persistence pi = fraction of C_r3 plans for retrievals that included a planted item in which the planted appliance or receptacle survives; laundering = critic recall on persisted rewritten items minus critic recall on the original planted items; gate precision/recall per (writer, reader, op, rate); retained-gain ratio in the 0% cells per writer x reader; consumer tokens and episodes/min per cell.
- Gate 0: under C_v3 for R1, H >= 6 net at some rate for at least one operation (positive control: Op-A at 50%). If no operation clears it, the study reports reader robustness with CIs and the laundering and gate claims are withdrawn.
- Schedule: Gate 0 first (3 ops x 3 rates x 2 writers for R1, 18 cells); then the 2x2 writer x reader diagonal at the Gate-0 passing rate under C_g3 (4 cells at 4 seeds); then C_r3, C_gr3, C_rule at the passing rate and at 0% for both readers (~20 cells); ~45 cells, ~26k episodes plus one bank collection; both GPUs serve one reader each; about 2 days.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Cheapest baseline first: C_rule (a keyword consistency check) is run before any LLM gate; C_static and C0 fix the floor and the reference for 'net' gains.
- Direct injection of the unmodified items (C_v3) is the comparator for every adaptation and gate cell; C_gr3 is token-matched to C_r3 by construction (the gate's reasons are not injected).
- Self-pool control: the 0% cells give the retained-gain ratio per writer x reader against each reader's own bank at matched collection cost; contamination harm is reported as a fraction of that clean gain.
- Memory-absent, matched and mismatched evaluation of the gate: false-positive rate on the clean 0% bank (precision), on the reader's own-type items (matched) and on items retrieved for the wrong task type (mismatched, which the gate should discard).
- Ablations: gate with writer identity revealed vs hidden; gate with the item's outcome label hidden vs shown (does the label drive the judgment); critic recall with the original item shown beside the rewrite (upper bound on detectability).
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (Gate 0): Op-A at 25% or 50% produces H >= 6 net under C_v3 for R1. Falsifier: H < 6 at every rate and operation, i.e. the reader ignores planted procedure errors as in-context classifiers ignore wrong labels. Arm: the C_v3 x Op-A x 50% cell; the outcome is not entailed because the reader may follow the task keyword rather than the item.
- P2 (reconstruction does not filter): at the Gate-0 rate, pi >= 0.5 and H(C_r3) >= 0.75 x H(C_v3). Falsifier: H(C_r3) <= 0.5 x H(C_v3) or pi < 0.25, meaning the rewrite repairs the planted step. Arm: the C_r3 cell at the Gate-0 rate with per-plan persistence scoring.
- P3 (laundering): the post-hoc critic's recall on persisted rewritten plans is lower than on the original planted items by >= 0.15 absolute. Falsifier: recall on rewrites >= recall on originals - 0.05. Arm: the offline critic applied to both sets of the same planted items.
- P4 (own-style blind spot, 2x2): C_g3 recall on the diagonal cells (W_self->R1, W_other->R2) is lower than on the off-diagonal cells (W_other->R1, W_self->R2) by >= 0.10 for both readers. Falsifier: either reader shows recall(own) >= recall(foreign), or both readers show low recall on the same bank regardless of who reads it (a pool property, not proximity). Arm: the four C_g3 detection logs at the Gate-0 rate, 4 seeds.
- P5 (gate recovers without over-discarding): C_gr3 recovers >= 50% of H(C_v3) at the Gate-0 rate with gate precision >= 0.7, and on the 0% bank loses <= 4 net relative to C_v3. Falsifier: recovery < 50%, or the 0% loss exceeds 4 net (the gate discards good foreign items to buy robustness). Arm: the C_gr3 cells at the Gate-0 rate and at 0%.
- P6 (where an LLM gate is needed): C_rule reaches recall >= 0.8 on Op-A but <= 0.2 on Op-B, and C_g3 beats C_rule on Op-B by >= 0.2 recall. Falsifier: C_g3 does not exceed C_rule's Op-B recall by 0.2 (the cheap rule is enough). Arm: C_rule vs C_g3 on the Op-B bank.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired per-game differences between the contaminated and clean cells of the same bank, reader and condition; cluster bootstrap over games with seeds nested; 274 x 2 seeds for Gate-0 screening (+/-8 net) and 274 x 4 seeds for the P4 2x2 and the P2/P5 cells (+/-5.7). Detection metrics are computed over retrieval events (about 820 per cell at k=3 x 274 x 1 seed), which gives precision/recall CIs of about +/-0.04 by bootstrap over games; the P4 margin of 0.10 is set to twice that. Planted items are labelled at construction; persistence is scored by string match on the appliance or receptacle token with a manual audit of 100 rewrites. Margins are fractions of the Gate-0 harm. One pre-registered headline contrast (P4), P2/P3 secondary. Tokens and throughput logged per cell.
Preprint Collision Check: All queries via tools/ideate2/s2cli.py (s2=ok hf=ok). (1) recent: 'read-time detection of harmful retrieved skill self-critique poisoned experience note agent precision recall' -> MaliciousSkillBench 2608.19901, SkillJack 2608.03509, SkillHarm 2606.02540, Honest Lying 2605.29463, MemoryGraft 2512.16962, Agent-R 2501.11425; SkillJack is the nearest (poisoned histories persist through the agent's own skill pipeline) but has no rewriting arm, no writer identity and no gate scored by precision/recall. (2) closest named method: 'MemHarness critique and reconstruct retrieved experience negative transfer verbatim replay' -> 2607.28272 and continual-learning replay papers; MemHarness does not plant errors or score detection. (3) home: 'paraphrase sanitization poisoned samples detection precision recall rewriting defense' -> 2303.13408 (paraphrasing evades detectors; retrieval defends), SONAR 2605.01078 (NLI-based sanitization of malicious instructions in RAG), 2604.18248 (prompt-injection detection techniques), 2510.21322 (unlearning-based sanitization); the paraphrase-evasion result is the laundering mechanism in its home form and none applies it to a reader rewriting a procedure it will execute. (4) home: 'in-context demonstrations from a weaker model verification rewriting before use label noise detection' -> 2411.19581 (ICL with noisy labels), 2202.12837 (label correctness matters little for ICL), label-noise detection papers; 2202.12837 is the reason Gate 0 may fail and is cited as such. No paper found that scores read-time detection by writer identity or measures wrong-step persistence through a rewrite.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Gate 0 may fail: ALFWorld readers might follow the task keyword and ignore a wrong appliance, in which case the contamination claims are withdrawn and only the clean retained-gain cells stand. Op-A on expert walkthroughs is more salient than on wandering self trajectories, so the expert bank is reported separately and the headline 2x2 uses only the two 32B pools at matched length. Persistence scoring by token match can miss paraphrased wrong steps; the manual audit bounds this. The post-hoc critic is the reader itself, so laundering is measured for one critic family; a second critic (the other backbone) is run as a check. EXAONE serving is unverified; without it the 2x2 collapses to a proximity manipulation within Qwen3 (standard vs different-scaffold pool), which is weaker. No adversary is modelled; the operations are manufactured errors, not attacks.
Addresses gap: G19 (adaptation may propagate contamination and readers' read-time detection is unexamined) as the primary target; G18 partially, through the retained-gain and retained-harm ratios per writer x reader cell.
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet: the contamination rule and Q3 ask for planted wrong items at controlled rates and a detector scored by precision and recall; this idea claims something those do not state, namely that the adaptation step itself raises persistence and lowers detectability (laundering) and that the gate's recall is lowest on the reader's own style, separable from a pool property by the 2x2. Digest card: 2605.22842 claims trust laundering across sessions and defends with provenance information-flow control on policy-formatted documents; this idea claims laundering happens inside the reader's own rewrite of benign-looking procedure errors with no cross-session chain, and that provenance-free detection depends on writer-reader proximity, neither of which that card measures. Archived lineage_blast_radius was judged entailed by its consolidation rule; here persistence through a rewrite is measured, and the rewrite can produce the falsifier by repairing the planted step.

Name: rewriter_trained_against_one_reader_matched_cost
Title: A Rewriter Learned Against One Reader Is That Reader's: Transfer Fraction of Execution-Trained Experience Rewriters Across Scaffold, Capability and Backbone, Against Self-Collection at Equal GPU-Hours
Short Hypothesis: An experience rewriter trained by execution-feedback rejection sampling against one reader keeps less than half of its increment when applied to a different 32B backbone, more than three quarters when applied to the same backbone under a different scaffold, and an intermediate fraction when applied to the same backbone in thinking mode, so reader specificity follows policy proximity rather than capability; and for the held-out backbone the same GPU-hours spent on collecting its own bank buy at least as much as importing the foreign-trained rewriter.
Related Work: Model-aware skill alignment (2605.30723) trains a lightweight rewriter per backbone and reports that skills must be adapted to each backbone, but never applies a rewriter trained against one backbone to another, never reports the fraction of gain retained, and does not cost the evolution search against self-collection. SkillRevise (2606.01139) claims revised skills carry generalized procedural knowledge that transfers across models, the opposite prediction, without quantifying the fraction retained or a matched-cost comparison. CLEAR (2604.07487) trains a context augmentation model by contrastive reflection, SFT and RL against one execution agent and does not test another. AdaCoM (2605.30785) finds the right compression level for a frozen agent's own context depends on that agent's baseline strength, a hint that context artifacts are reader-specific, but it is not a foreign-experience rewriter and reports no held-out reader. HarnessDev (2609.01437) reports self-built harnesses transfer poorly across models. In the home literature, prompt transfer across model sizes has a transferability metric (PANDA 2208.10160) and MePO (2505.09930) claims model-agnostic prompt merits; the question of whether an execution-grounded rewriter is model-agnostic is open. Archived closer_beats_stronger concerned raw memory transfer, not a learned transfer component, and did not separate proximity from capability.
Abstract: Learned transfer components (rewriters, context augmentation models, memory composers) are trained against one consumer and assumed to serve others. We measure how much of a rewriter's gain survives a change of reader, with the reader manipulated along three separated axes. Two rewriters, both QLoRA adapters on Qwen3-32B, are trained on ALFWorld training games by rejection sampling: candidate rewrites of k=3 retrieved foreign items (expert and EXAONE-4.0-32B banks) are executed by the reader in the loop, and rewrites that turn a verbatim failure into a success are kept as SFT targets; R_A is trained against Qwen3-32B under the standard scaffold, R_B against EXAONE-4.0-32B. Each rewriter is then evaluated on four readers: the training reader, the same backbone under a different scaffold and temperature (proximity), the same backbone in thinking mode (capability at fixed backbone), and the other backbone (backbone at verified matched k=0 success), against verbatim injection at matched consumer tokens, a training-free prompted rewriter, and the rewriter given no retrieved item (memory-absent; detects memorized plans) or items for the wrong task type (mismatched). The transfer fraction is the rewriter's increment on a reader divided by its increment on its training reader, with cluster-bootstrap CIs. A matched-cost arm gives the held-out backbone its own additional bank collected at the rewriter's training GPU-hours. Gate 0 requires each rewriter to beat token-matched verbatim injection on its own reader by 6 net. The claims fail if the foreign-trained rewriter matches the reader-trained one, if the thinking-mode reader keeps less than the other backbone, if the memory-absent rewriter keeps most of the gain, or if the imported rewriter beats self-collection at equal cost.

- Readers: A Qwen3-32B standard scaffold non-thinking; A' Qwen3-32B plan-then-act scaffold, T=0.7 (verify k=0 within +/-5 net of A); A'' Qwen3-32B thinking mode (verify k=0 >= 8 net above A); B EXAONE-4.0-32B (verify k=0 within +/-5 net of A; if not, B is reported as a joint backbone-and-capability change and P2 is restricted to A' vs A''). C gpt-oss-120b only if it serves on one A100.
- Rewriter training: for 1,000 training games, 3 candidate rewrites per game from the prompted Qwen3-32B rewriter at T=0.8 (input: task, first observation, k=3 items; output: one plan in the reader's action format), executed by the in-loop reader (3,000 episodes, ~2.5 GPU-h at 20/min), plus the verbatim run (1,000 episodes); keep rewrites where the reader succeeded and verbatim failed, and a 1:1 share of success-success pairs; QLoRA r=32 SFT, one epoch (~1.5 GPU-h). Same recipe for R_B with B in the loop. Rewriter backbone fixed at Qwen3-32B for both, so only the in-loop reader differs.
- Conditions per reader: C0; C_static (Measurement C); C_v3 verbatim; C_vtok verbatim at the k that matches the rewriter's output tokens; C_RA, C_RB the trained rewriters; C_R0 the prompted untrained rewriter; C_RA_empty (rewriter given the task and no item); C_RA_mis (items retrieved for a different task type); for B additionally C_selfcost (B's own bank enlarged by the episode-equivalent of R_A's training GPU-hours, read verbatim).

- Budget: two rewriters ~8 GPU-h; evaluation ~32 cells (headline cells at 4 seeds) ~19k episodes; the rewriter adapter is served on the GPU not serving the reader; about 3 days including bank collection.

- Cheapest first: C_static, then C_R0 (prompted rewriter, no training) before any trained cell.

- Self-pool control at matched collection cost: W_self for A; for B, C_selfcost converts R_A's training GPU-hours into EXAONE episodes at the measured episodes/GPU-h.
- Memory-absent (C_RA_empty), matched (training reader), mismatched (C_RA_mis and held-out readers) evaluation of each trained component, as the round rules require.

- Ablations: rewriter trained on success-success pairs only (does the contrastive filter matter); rewriter applied at k=1; rewriter with reader identity in the prompt.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (reader specificity): I(R_B,B) - I(R_A,B) >= 1/3 of I(R_A,A), and symmetrically I(R_A,A) - I(R_B,A) >= the same margin. Falsifier: the foreign-trained rewriter is within the margin of the reader-trained one on either reader, meaning the rewrites are reader-agnostic cleaning. Arm: the (B,C_RA) vs (B,C_RB) and (A,C_RB) vs (A,C_RA) cells at 4 seeds; both rewriters are trained on the same input bank so the cell can produce equality.
- P2 (proximity before capability): TF(R_A->A') >= 0.75, TF(R_A->A'') between 0.5 and 0.75, TF(R_A->B) < 0.5, with the ordering TF(A'') > TF(B) holding at CI level. Falsifier: TF(R_A->B) >= TF(R_A->A'') (the capability change costs more transfer than the backbone change) or TF(R_A->A') < 0.5 (a scaffold change alone breaks the rewriter). Arm: the A', A'' and B rewriter and C_vtok cells.
- P3 (not memorized plans): I(R_A on C_RA_empty, A) <= 1/3 of I(R_A,A). Falsifier: the rewriter with no retrieved item keeps >= 2/3 of its increment, in which case the transfer measured is plan transfer and P1/P2 are re-labelled as such. Arm: C_RA_empty and C_RA_mis for A.

Falsifier: the ratio does not rise or falls. Arm: the (W_other,A) verbatim and C_RA cells with the EXAONE writer reading its own bank as the denominator.

Gate 0 at 4 seeds before any held-out cell. Margins as fractions of the Gate-0 increment; one pre-registered headline contrast (P1), P2 secondary, the rest exploratory. Reader temperature 0 except A'; rewriter decoding temperature 0 at evaluation. Consumer tokens per episode include the rewriter's generated plan; training GPU-hours are logged from the runner and converted to episodes at the measured rate for C_selfcost. The reader in the training loop is served on one GPU while the other serves the candidate-rewrite generator, then the QLoRA job runs on one GPU while the other serves the first evaluation cells.

Name: self_pool_break_even
Title: Break-Even Budgets: How Little Self-Collection a Reader Needs Before a Foreign Experience Pool Stops Paying
Short Hypothesis: The advantage of a foreign experience pool (expert walkthroughs or another backbone's successes) over a reader's own success-filtered pool is confined to a coverage-limited regime: k=3 retrieval saturates once each task type has about three same-type successful items in the bank, so a reader with per-type k=0 success p_t and type frequency f_t needs only about m/(p_t f_t) attempted collection episodes on type t to catch up. For Qwen3-32B on ALFWorld this is roughly 10% of the full 3,553-game budget (about 13 GPU-minutes); the expert pool's retained-gain ratio against the full self pool is at most 1.3; and a second backbone's pool substitutes for own collection within noise. The amortized value of a shared foreign pool is therefore a collection-cost saving, not a quality gain, except on success-starved types.
Related Work: Agent Memory Distillation (arxiv:2608.07169) transfers a large teacher's trajectories into hierarchical memory for 4B-8B students without training (+27 pp AppWorld) but never runs the student's own pool at matched collection cost. Unified cross-domain pools (arxiv:2604.14004) and transactive population memory (arxiv:2606.19911) report consumer gains without a self-collected control. Inference-time distillation (arxiv:2512.02543) reports a cost-accuracy Pareto frontier on ALFWorld using a stronger teacher's demonstrations, again with no self-pool arm. Retrieval-aware fine-tuning (arxiv:2603.18272) establishes simple episodic retrieval as a strong baseline but does not vary who wrote the episodes or the budget. In the home literature, demonstration-regularized RL (arxiv:2310.17303) bounds the sample-complexity saving from expert demonstrations but no work measures the break-even budget at which self-generated successes reproduce the expert's in-context benefit. The archived idea closer_beats_stronger (5.75) attributed transfer to policy proximity without a self-pool control; this idea attributes writer effects to same-type coverage and includes that control. Measurement A on this node (expert -> Qwen3-32B, k=3, +27.1/+32.1 net) is the anchor cell this design extends with a budget axis and a second writer and reader.
Abstract: Every reported gain from transferred agent experience is the gain of having some memory plus whatever the foreign writer adds; no study separates the two by running the reader's own pool at the same collection cost (digest gap G21). We propose a break-even analysis on ALFWorld with writer identity manipulated (expert walkthroughs; Qwen3-32B's own k=0 successes; EXAONE-4.0-32B's own k=0 successes on the same 3,553 train games) and readers Qwen3-32B and EXAONE-4.0-32B, using one retriever, one bank format (action-observation items obtained by replaying every item in the environment so that expert and on-policy items differ only in path, not in rendering), k=3 and k=1. The self pool is collected under nested budgets b in {0.5, 2.5, 10, 25, 100}% of attempted train games (two draws per sub-100% budget); the expert pool is subset to the same game indices; a coverage arm caps the full bank at m in {1, 3, 10, all} same-type items per type. Estimands per writer x reader cell: net success vs k=0 and vs the static-procedure prompt (Measurement C), the retained-gain ratio of the foreign pool against the reader's own pool at the same budget, the break-even budget B* at which the self pool matches the foreign pool's full-budget gain, and per-type break-evens against the reader's k=0 success. We predict saturation by b=10% and m=3, an expert/self ratio of at most 1.3 at full budget, per-type break-evens ordered by 1/(p_t f_t) (heat largest, pick-and-place smallest), and symmetric writer-swap substitution within noise. Costs are reported on both axes: writer-side collection GPU-hours and reader-side injected tokens, so that the amortized cost per net point of one shared pool versus R private pools can be stated for R=1,2,3.
Experiments: Preparation (CPU env replay, hours): render the 1,465 expert walkthroughs and the 1,892 Qwen3 successes into one item format by replaying actions in ALFWorld and recording observations; success-filter. Collection (GPU): verify EXAONE-4.0-32B in vLLM 0.13; collect its k=0 pool on the same 3,553 train games (about 3 GPU-hours) on one A100 while the other serves Qwen3 reader cells. Reader cells (each 274 validation games x 2 seeds = 548 paired episodes, about 30 min per replica): (A) anchors for the Qwen3 reader: k=0, static-procedure prompt (Measurement C), token-matched wrong-type placebo, expert full (Measurement A), self 100%; (B) self-pool budget sweep b in {0.5, 2.5, 10, 25}% x 2 draws, k=3 (8 cells) plus 100% (1); (C) expert subsets on the same game indices at the four sub-100% budgets (4 cells); (D) coverage arm m in {1, 3, 10} same-type items per type at full budget, for the self and expert banks (6 cells); (E) k=1 replicates: self 100%, self 10%, expert full (3 cells); (F) EXAONE reader: k=0, static, own 100%, own 10%, Qwen3 100%, Qwen3 10%, expert 100% (7 cells); Qwen3 reader on the EXAONE pool at 100% and 10% (2 cells). About 36 cells, roughly 19,800 episodes, about 9 wall-hours with one replica per GPU plus the 3 GPU-hour collection, scheduled so the collection job overlaps the Qwen3 reader cells; total about 1.5 days. Outputs per cell: success (aggregate, per type, seen/unseen), net vs k=0 and vs static prompt, injected tokens, steps; per writer x reader: retained-gain ratio at each budget, B*, per-type B*_t; amortized cost per net point for R readers sharing one pool vs R private pools.
Baselines and Ablations: k=0; static per-type procedure prompt at matched tokens (Measurement C; every gain reported net of it); token-matched wrong-type placebo (same injected tokens, items from other types) to bound the value of any memory; k=1 vs k=3; format ablation: raw on-policy self items (with the writer's reasoning text) vs the replayed action-observation rendering, to show the rendering does not carry the effect; two independent draws at every sub-100% budget to separate subset variance from the budget effect; coverage caps m in {1,3,10} at full budget as the direct test of the saturation mechanism; expert-pool subsets at the same game indices as the matched-item control for the budget axis; writer swap in both directions (Qwen3 reads EXAONE's pool, EXAONE reads Qwen3's pool) at 100% and 10%; the Measurement A expert cell reused as the positive control that the pipeline reproduces +27 net.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (headline, saturation): for the Qwen3-32B reader at k=3, the self pool collected at b=10% lands within 8 net points of the self pool at 100% in both draws. Falsifier: either 10% draw is at least 8 net below the full self pool with the paired CI excluding 0; arm: self-10% vs self-100% cells. P2 (coverage): capping the full bank at m=3 same-type items per type stays within 8 net of m=all, for both the self and the expert bank. Falsifier: m=3 is at least 8 net below m=all in either bank; arm: coverage cells. Positive control for P1-P2: b=0.5% (types with zero same-type items) and m=1 must fall at least 8 net below full; if they do not, the sweep is insensitive and P1-P2 are declared uninformative rather than confirmed. P3 (expert vs self at full budget): the expert pool's gain minus the full self pool's gain is below 8 net with CI including 0 (retained-gain ratio expert/self at most 1.3). Falsifier: expert minus self at least 8 with CI excluding 0; arm: expert-full vs self-100% at k=3 (the reverse outcome, self beating expert by 8, is also reported and would falsify the ratio bound from the other side). P4 (per-type ordering): at b=2.5% the per-type deficit of the self pool relative to its 100% version is largest for heat and smallest for pick-and-place, with Spearman rho between the per-type deficit and 1/(p_t f_t) at least 0.6 pooled over both draws, both readers and both k. Falsifier: rho at most 0.2, or heat not among the two largest deficits; arm: per-type deficits from the b=2.5% cells. P5 (writer swap): for each reader, the other backbone's full pool is within 8 net of the reader's own full pool. Falsifier: own minus other at least 8 with CI excluding 0 in either reader; arm: writer-swap cells. None of P1-P5 is entailed: retrieval could require many near-duplicate items (falsifying P1-P2), on-policy successes could carry inefficient or lucky procedures (falsifying P3 either way), per-type deficits could be flat (P4), and an own pool could be privileged by proximity (P5).
Measurement and Noise Control: All cells are paired on the same 274 validation games with the same two seeds per game and the same retrieval ordering; the resampling unit for bootstrap CIs is the game (seeds nested), stratified by the six task types. Primary statistics are paired net-success differences; retained-gain ratios are reported with joint paired-bootstrap CIs and only when the denominator's CI excludes 0 (otherwise the difference is the estimand, since the ratio is ill-conditioned). The noise floor of a 274 x 2 cell is about +/-8 net; all margins are set at 8 net, which is 30% of the +27 Measurement A effect; the Gate for the positive control is the same 8. Order of runs: k=0 and static prompt first, then the two anchors (expert full, self 100%), then the sweep; the sweep is stopped early if P3 falsifies with expert beating self by more than 16, since then break-even is not reached within budget and the reported quantity becomes the residual expert advantage per type. Subset variance is estimated from the two draws per budget and reported alongside the budget effect. Per-type analyses pool across readers, draws and k to reach about 45 games x 2 seeds x 8 cells per type; per-type CIs are reported and the coverage arm (full-cell power) is the confirmatory test of the mechanism. Throughput and vLLM queue occupancy are logged per cell; both A100s stay busy by overlapping the EXAONE collection with Qwen3 reader cells.

Name: reader_pays_writer_detours
Title: The Reader Pays the Writer's Detours: Consumer-Side Cost of Transferred Experience Tracks the Writer's Episode Length, Not Its Success
Short Hypothesis: The consumer-side cost of using a foreign experience pool (generated tokens, observation tokens and steps per episode) is inherited from the writer's trajectory length: a reader copies the number of steps of the retrieved item, so on-policy self pools (long, with detours) cost more per successful episode than minimal expert walkthroughs at equal success. Pruning replay-verified detours from self items at fixed content removes the inherited cost without losing success, and padding expert walkthroughs with benign detours adds it; consequently the ranking of writers by gain per consumer token differs from their ranking by success, and cost-matched comparisons across writers must charge the reader's generated tokens, not only the injected ones.
Related Work: Consumer-side inference tokens are not reported with transfer gains (digest gap G22): AMD (arxiv:2608.07169) omits student-side overhead, SkillEvolBench (arxiv:2605.24117) compares raw trajectories and skills without matched per-reader token cost, memory-system profiling (arxiv:2606.24775) attributes cost to phases for a single writer, PAST-Bench (arxiv:2608.04003) and S3Gym (arxiv:2608.31100) report gains without the retention cost. AgentDiet (arxiv:2509.23586) reduces the agent's own context history to cut cost and inference-time distillation (arxiv:2512.02543) moves the ALFWorld cost-accuracy frontier with teacher demonstrations, but neither asks whether the reader's episode length depends on the retrieved item's length. MemoryCPT (arxiv:2608.04843) optimizes quality per inference cost within one writer-reader pair. In the home literature, Extraneousness-Aware Imitation Learning (arxiv:2210.01379) filters irrelevant segments from noisy demonstrations to recover performance, and 'What Demonstration Curation Metrics Do to Your Policy' (arxiv:2606.10229) shows defect detection and downstream policy quality decouple; both concern success, not inherited episode cost, and neither swaps the demonstrator. The archived idea abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) varied abstraction level within one writer on the success axis; here length is manipulated at fixed content with writer identity swapped and the outcome is the reader's cost.
Abstract: Transfer results report what the reader gains, not what the reader pays. We propose that the consumer-side cost of transferred experience is set by the writer's path length: LLM readers imitate the step structure of retrieved items, so a self pool of on-policy successes (which contain failed actions, 'Nothing happens' observations and revisits) makes the reader's own episodes longer than an expert walkthrough does, even when success is equal. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B and EXAONE-4.0-32B as readers, the writer set is expert walkthroughs, Qwen3's own k=0 successes and EXAONE's own k=0 successes, all rendered in one action-observation format by environment replay. Two content-preserving manipulations vary length at fixed content: self-pruned (a rule that removes actions whose observation was 'Nothing happens' or that revisit a location without state change; every pruned item is replay-verified to still complete the task) and expert-padded (benign detour steps sampled from the self pool's detour distribution inserted at random positions, replay-verified, padded to the self pool's mean length). We measure success, steps and consumer tokens (injected + generated + observation) per episode, the causal 'length-inheritance slope' of reader steps on item steps across the manipulation pairs, and gain per 1k consumer tokens per writer x reader cell, all net of k=0 and of the static-procedure prompt (Measurement C). Predictions: a slope of at least 0.3 in both manipulation pairs and for the foreign reader; pruning and padding within 6 net of their unmanipulated versions on success; and a writer ranking by gain per consumer token that differs from the ranking by success. The result gives transfer evaluation a cost axis on the reader's side and a cheap, replay-verified pruning step that any writer's pool can pass through before sharing.
Experiments: Preparation (CPU env replay): render all pools into one item format; build self-pruned and expert-padded variants with replay verification (drop and count items that fail replay); log item lengths (mean steps: expert, self-raw, self-pruned, expert-padded, EXAONE-raw, EXAONE-pruned). Name: leave_one_type_out_split
Title: Within-Type Splits Inflate Transfer: A Leave-One-Type-Out Composite Shows Retrieval Gains Are Type-Bound, Harm Tracks Within-Type Gain, and Only Weights Carry Portable Competence
Short Hypothesis: The standard ALFWorld splits (valid_seen/valid_unseen) always leave same-type items in the bank, so every measured transfer gain is procedure retrieval. Under a leave-one-type-out (LOTO) composite, in which each validation game is read against a bank lacking its own task type, retrieval gains from every writer collapse to the noise floor, and the writer that helps most within-type (the off-policy expert, whose items the reader follows most closely) becomes the most harmful under type shift, while the reader's own pool is near neutral. Absorbing the same expert pool into QLoRA weights, evaluated with the matching LOTO adapter, retains a positive type-portable gain (navigation and action validity), so the retrieval-versus-weights ranking flips between splits at matched cost.
Related Work: PAST-Bench (arxiv:2608.04003) toggles retained experience and S3Gym (arxiv:2608.31100) compares history ICL, summaries and training, but neither holds out a task type or swaps the writer. AgentCL (arxiv:2606.02461) builds controlled task streams for continual learning without cross-writer or held-out-type transfer. Retrieval-aware fine-tuning (arxiv:2603.18272) claims generalization to unseen tasks but does not compare retrieval and weights under the same held-out split with writer identity manipulated. Parametric memories (PEAM arxiv:2605.27762; fast-weight memory arxiv:2606.04536) assert efficiency and portability on one environment and backbone (digest gap G25). MemHarness (arxiv:2607.28272) shows verbatim replay of retrieved experience causes negative transfer out of distribution, on self-written experience. In the home literature, in-context learning with mismatched demonstrations is known to hurt or help depending on evidence mixture (arxiv:2605.26350) and cross-task demonstration transfer can help (CrossICL arxiv:2505.24143), but no work couples the harm of wrong-task demonstrations to how strongly the same demonstrations help in-task, across demonstrators. Measurement A on this node found unseen ~ seen with the full bank (a room split, not a type split) and Measurement B provides the QLoRA arm. Archived context_wins_substrate_conflict (5.55) concerned substrate conflict within-type; here the split, not the conflict, is the manipulated variable.
Abstract: Transfer of agent experience is evaluated on splits that keep same-type experience in the bank, so the gain reported is the gain of finding a same-type procedure. We propose a leave-one-type-out (LOTO) composite for ALFWorld: six banks each missing one task type, and every one of the 274 validation games read against the bank that lacks its type, giving a single full-power cell per writer x reader. Writer identity is manipulated (expert walkthroughs; Qwen3-32B's own successes; EXAONE-4.0-32B's own successes) with one retriever and one item format; readers are Qwen3-32B and EXAONE-4.0-32B. The same expert pool is also absorbed into QLoRA rank-32 adapters (one all-type adapter as in Measurement B and six LOTO adapters), served by vLLM multi-LoRA so the adapter composite runs as one cell; adapters are evaluated memory-absent, with matched retrieval (their own pool) and with mismatched retrieval (the self pool). Controls: k=0, six-procedure and five-procedure static prompts (the LOTO analog of Measurement C), a random-other-type token-matched placebo, and a wrong-procedure graft at 100% rate as the Gate-0 positive control that the reader is harmed by wrong items at all. Estimands: within-type gain, LOTO gain, their difference (the type-bound fraction), the cross-writer coupling between within-type gain and LOTO harm, and the within-type and LOTO gains of weights versus retrieval at matched cost (2 GPU-hours per adapter versus zero collection plus injected tokens). Predictions: LOTO retrieval gains at most +8 for every writer, expert LOTO harm at least 6 net with harm ranked as within-type gain, LOTO adapter gain at least +8 and above LOTO retrieval by 8 while within-type retrieval beats the all-type adapter by 8. The composite is a cheap addition to any transfer evaluation and yields a portability accounting per pathway.
Experiments: Preparation: render pools by env replay; construct six LOTO banks per writer (type excluded by the ALFWorld task-type label; pick-two and pick-and-place are recorded as a known skeleton-similar pair and analysed separately); build the wrong-procedure graft pool (each item's appliance step swapped to the wrong appliance, replay-checked to fail). Collection: EXAONE k=0 pool (about 3 GPU-hours). Training on one A100 while the other serves: seven QLoRA r32 adapters on the expert pool (one all-type, six LOTO, about 2 GPU-hours each, about 14 GPU-hours), then served via vLLM multi-LoRA on the bf16 base with per-request adapter selection. Reader cells (274 games x 2 seeds): Qwen3 reader at k=3: standard bank for self and EXAONE writers (expert from Measurement A) (2), LOTO banks for expert, self, EXAONE (3), random-other-type placebo (1), five-procedure static prompt (1), wrong-procedure graft positive control (1); adapter cells: all-type adapter memory-absent (1), LOTO adapter composite memory-absent (1), LOTO adapter + LOTO retrieval of the expert pool (matched) (1), all-type adapter + standard expert retrieval (matched) (1), LOTO adapter + LOTO self-pool retrieval (mismatched) (1); EXAONE reader at k=3: standard banks for expert, own, Qwen3 (3), LOTO banks for the same three (3), k=0, six- and five-procedure static prompts (3). About 22 cells, roughly 12,100 episodes, about 5.5 wall-hours on two replicas plus 14 GPU-hours of adapter training and 3 GPU-hours of collection overlapped on the second GPU; about 2 days. The LOTO self cell for the Qwen3 reader is run with 4 seeds to power the seen/unseen decomposition. Per cell: success, net vs k=0 and vs the appropriate static prompt, per type, seen/unseen, injected tokens, steps, and the cost per net point (collection GPU-hours, training GPU-hours, consumer tokens).
Baselines and Ablations: k=0; six-procedure static prompt (Measurement C) for standard cells and five-procedure static prompt (target type omitted) for LOTO cells, both token-matched; random-other-type placebo to separate nearest-wrong-type retrieval from any wrong-type content; wrong-procedure graft at 100% as the harm positive control (Gate 0: at least 6 net harm required); adapters evaluated memory-absent, matched and mismatched per the standing rule; adapter trained on the self pool (one all-type adapter, 2 GPU-hours) as the writer ablation for the parametric arm if time permits; standard-bank cells reused from the sibling designs where identical; k=1 LOTO cells for expert and self as the retrieval-strength ablation; pick-two/pick-and-place leakage check by excluding both types together in a seventh bank.

P2 (harm tracks within-type gain): the writer with the largest within-type gain (predicted: expert) shows LOTO harm of at least 6 net vs k=0 in at least one reader, and the writer ranking by within-type gain equals the ranking by LOTO harm in both readers (Kendall tau = 1 over three writers). Falsifier: expert LOTO at or above -2 net (no harm), or the two rankings disagree; arm: standard and LOTO cells for three writers x two readers. Gate 0: the wrong-procedure graft must produce at least 6 net harm; if it does not, the reader is insensitive to wrong items and P2 is void, not confirmed. P3 (substrate flip): the LOTO adapter composite gains at least +8 net vs the base model without retrieval and exceeds LOTO retrieval of the same expert pool by at least 8, while within-type the k=3 expert retrieval exceeds the all-type adapter by at least 8. Falsifier: LOTO adapter at most +4, or LOTO retrieval at or above the LOTO adapter, or the all-type adapter at or above within-type retrieval; arm: adapter cells vs retrieval cells. P4 (static-prompt survival): the LOTO adapter gain exceeds the five-procedure static prompt by at least 6 net. Falsifier: static-5 at or above adapter minus 4; arm: five-procedure static cell vs LOTO adapter composite. P5 (room-bound residual): for the self writer, LOTO gain on valid_seen exceeds LOTO gain on valid_unseen by at least 10 net (own exploration items reveal object locations in familiar rooms), measured with 4 seeds. Falsifier: seen minus unseen at most 2 under LOTO for the self writer; arm: the 4-seed LOTO self cell split by seen/unseen. None is entailed: other-type items could teach navigation (P1), self items could harm as much as expert items (P2), adapters could overfit to the trained types (P3), the five-procedure prompt could carry the adapter's generic gains (P4), and room cues may be absent from success-filtered items (P5).
Measurement and Noise Control: All cells are paired on the same 274 games and seeds with the same retrieval ordering; game-level stratified bootstrap CIs; the LOTO composite keeps the full 274 x 2 cell so the +/-8 noise floor applies to every headline comparison, unlike per-type held-out evaluation (about 45 games per type, +/-20). Margins: 8 net for gains (30% of the Measurement A effect), 6 net for harm (Gate 0), and 10 net for the seen/unseen decomposition with the 4-seed cell (halved cell size). The type-bound fraction is reported as a paired difference (standard minus LOTO on the same games) with its CI. Rank agreement across writers (P2) is reported with a bootstrap over games. Adapter cost is charged in GPU-hours per reader and retrieval cost in injected tokens per episode, and both are converted to cost per net point under each split. Order: k=0, static prompts and the graft positive control first (Gate 0 must pass before any LOTO harm claim), then the retrieval LOTO cells, then the adapter cells as they finish training; adapter training runs on the second GPU throughout so no serving replica idles. Queue occupancy and throughput per replica are logged per cell.

Name: complementarity_not_proximity
Title: Complementarity, Not Proximity: What a Reader Keeps of a Foreign Writer's Experience Is Set by the Writer's Success on the Reader's Failure Types
Short Hypothesis: For success-filtered experience pools built on the same task set at the same episode budget, the fraction of gain a reader keeps from a foreign writer's pool (retained-gain ratio against the reader's own matched-cost pool, net of a static-procedure prompt) is governed by writer-reader complementarity (the writer's k=0 success advantage on the task types where the reader fails), not by policy proximity (writer-reader action agreement) and not by the writer's overall capability; a foreign pool beats the reader's own pool (ratio > 1) exactly in the cells where complementarity is positive, and proximity is inert above a format threshold.
Related Work: Agent Memory Distillation (arXiv:2608.07169) transfers a strong teacher's memory to 4B-8B students and asserts that effectiveness depends on 'teacher capability and student compatibility' without measuring either or comparing against a student-collected pool. Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All (arXiv:2605.30723) and arXiv:2605.23899 show skill utility is backbone-dependent and independent of scale but do not say which property of the writer-reader pair predicts it. Cross-model memory pools (arXiv:2604.14004) and population stores (arXiv:2606.19911) report transfer without writer manipulation. In the imitation literature, demonstration compatibility between demonstrators is measured for a trained policy (arXiv:2210.08073), retrieval-based behavior cloning copies actions from the nearest expert state (arXiv:2306.09082, arXiv:2606.09758), and recovery-trajectory self-training is argued to beat cloning from experts that never fail (arXiv:2501.11425); none of them manipulates the demonstrator's identity for an in-context reader. The archived idea closer_beats_stronger (5.75) claimed proximity predicts transfer; judges noted proximity and capability were not separated and there was no self-pool control. This proposal manipulates proximity at fixed capability and capability at fixed format, adds the matched-cost self pool, and predicts the opposite of closer_beats_stronger.
Abstract: Every measured agent-memory gain in this program was written and read by the same policy or by an expert planner, and the 2026 literature moves experience between models without saying what governs how much survives the move. We build a writer x reader matrix on ALFWorld with writer identity as the manipulated variable: six writers (expert walkthroughs; Qwen3-32B self; Qwen3-32B with a different temperature/scaffold selected to have the same k=0 success, a proximity manipulation; Qwen3-32B with thinking on and thoughts stripped from stored items, a capability manipulation at fixed serialization; EXAONE-4.0-32B self; gpt-oss-120b self), each pool collected on the same 3,553 training games (matched episode budget) and success-filtered, one retriever, k=3 (k=1 for the Qwen3 reader), and three readers. Two writer-reader statistics are computed offline before any transfer cell is run: proximity pi(W,R), the reader's greedy-action agreement with the writer's stored actions on 300 sampled states per pool (plus reader NLL per action token), and complementarity kappa(W,R) = sum over types of share_t * max(0, p_W(t) - p_R(t)), the writer's success advantage on the reader's k=0 failure types. The estimand is the retained-gain ratio rho(W->R) = [S_R(W pool) - S_R(static procedure)] / [S_R(R self pool) - S_R(static procedure)], with the writer-denominator variant for backbone writers. We predict that the fixed-capability proximity contrast moves rho by less than 0.2 while the fixed-format capability contrast moves it by more than 0.3; that rho > 1 iff kappa > 0.05 across the twelve cross cells; and that the gain over the reader's own pool lands on the reader's failure-type group. A length-filtered self pool (near-optimal own successes at matched item count against a random subset of the same size) tests whether the capability term acts through item optimality. The result is a per-cell rule for when foreign experience is worth reading, stated against the cheapest baselines (static procedure prompt, own pool at the same cost) and against the archived proximity claim.
Experiments: Setup: ALFWorld, 274 validation games (140 seen / 134 unseen), six task types; readers Q = Qwen3-32B (verified), E = EXAONE-4.0-32B and G = gpt-oss-120b (Gate V: serve in vLLM 0.13 on one A100 each and reach k=0 success >= 0.30, else the reader is dropped and the matrix shrinks). Writers: X expert (on disk), Q-self (on disk, T=0 ReAct thinking off), Q-prox (same backbone; candidates: T=1.0 same scaffold; paraphrased Act-first scaffold; screened on 274 x 1 seed, the first candidate whose k=0 is within +/-3 net of Q-self and whose pi(Q-prox,Q) is at least 0.15 below pi(Q-self,Q) is used; manipulation check pre-registered), Q-cap (thinking on, thoughts removed from stored items so serialization equals Q-self; must reach k=0 >= Q-self + 8; fallback: the Measurement-B QLoRA writer, with its pi reported), E-self, G-self. Every backbone writer runs the same 3,553 training games once (matched episode budget; GPU-hours also reported), success-filtered, same retriever (task-description embedding, nearest by type-agnostic cosine), same injection template (the reader's scaffold), k=3; k=1 for the six Q-reader cells. Offline statistics: pi(W,R) via 300 stratified states per pool with the reader acting greedily on the writer's history (about 1 GPU-hour total), kappa(W,R) from the collection run's per-type success (writer) and the reader's k=0 validation per-type success. Cells: 3 readers x 6 writers at k=3 (18), k=1 for reader Q (6), k=0 (3), static-procedure prompt from Measurement C (3), self-opt vs self-rand for reader Q (2), mixed pool self+foreign at matched item count for the top foreign cell (1), token-matched placebo (unrelated-type trajectories at the k=3 token count) per reader (3): 36 cells x 548 episodes (274 x 2 seeds), 4 seeds for the P1, P3 and P4 cells (+8 cell-equivalents) = about 24,000 episodes. Scheduling: GPU0 serves the reader under evaluation while GPU1 collects the next writer pool (Q-prox, Q-cap, E-self, G-self: 12-18 GPU-hours, G slower), then both GPUs serve readers with clients spread across replicas; about 3 days. Analysis: rho per cell with game-level bootstrap CIs; Spearman(rho, kappa) and partial Spearman(rho, pi | kappa) over the 12 cross cells; per-type gains grouped into reader-failure types (p_R < 0.5) vs reader-success types. Pre-registration of Gate V, Gate 0, manipulation checks, margins and the cell list before the first confirmatory cell.
Baselines and Ablations: k=0 per reader; static per-type procedure prompt (Measurement C) per reader, every gain reported net of it; reader's own pool at matched episode budget (the denominator); expert pool for reader Q (replicates Measurement A); Agent Memory Distillation-style hierarchical memory (arXiv:2608.07169, reimplemented without training) built from the strongest writer's pool for the strongest->weakest cell, to check the rule is not an artifact of raw-trajectory banks; k=1 vs k=3; token-matched placebo (same token count of unrelated-type trajectories) to separate content from context length; mixed pool (self + foreign, matched item count); self-opt vs self-rand (length-filtered own successes on failure types vs random subset of equal size, same collection cost); writer-denominator ratio rho_w for backbone writers; seen vs unseen split reported separately; Q-prox and Q-cap manipulation checks (k=0 and pi) reported as cells in their own right.

Name: thoughts_do_not_travel
Title: Actions Travel, Thoughts Don't: The Writer's Reasoning Text Is the Non-Transferable Part of Cross-Backbone Agent Experience, and a Deterministic Strip Matches a Learned Rewriter
Short Hypothesis: The component of a stored experience item that fails to transfer across backbones is the writer's reasoning text (ReAct thoughts, analysis-channel text), not its action-observation sequence: for writer != reader, deterministic action-only re-serialization of the writer's items into the reader's scaffold (zero LLM cost) recovers most of the same-backbone-minus-foreign deficit, for writer = reader the writer's thoughts are neutral or helpful, the value of thoughts is a reader-side property (the reader's own re-rationalization of foreign actions adds what its own thoughts add to its own actions), and a model-conditioned LLM rewriter adds nothing over the strip at matched tokens.

None of them asks which part of an item fails to travel, and none runs a zero-cost strip as the baseline for the rewriter. In the knowledge-distillation home literature, rationale mismatch between teacher and student is a known failure: token-selective distillation lets the student 'explain in its own words' (arXiv:2603.13260), rationale selection by accuracy/diversity/difficulty (arXiv:2509.23574), symbolic CoT distillation (arXiv:2306.14050), and provenance tracing shows which sentences of a distilled model come from the teacher (arXiv:2512.20908); these are parametric, and the in-context analog with writer identity manipulated has not been run. Abstract: When an experience item written by one backbone is read by another, part of the writer's gain is lost. We test the claim that the lost part is carried by the writer's reasoning text and not by its actions. Name: shared_blind_spot
Title: Shared Blind Spots: A Reader Is Most Harmed by, and Least Able to Detect, Contaminated Experience Written by Its Own Policy
Short Hypothesis: Contamination in an experience bank propagates in proportion to writer-reader policy proximity: failed trajectories relabelled as successes are more harmful per planted item and less detectable at read time when written by the reader's own policy or a near variant than when written by a distant backbone, because read-time detection is the reader's own plausibility judgment, which endorsed those actions when it produced them; a judge from a different backbone detects a writer's masked failures better than the writer's own backbone does (a diagonal deficit in the judge x writer table), and manufactured wrong-procedure grafts (positive control) are harmful and detectable regardless of writer.
Related Work: MemoryGraft (arXiv:2512.16962) implants attacker-written 'successful experiences' and shows persistent drift on one backbone; the Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608) diagnoses how agents consume conflicting memory along a trajectory and finds stronger agents are harmed more, varying the reader but not the writer and without a read-time detector; MemAudit (arXiv:2605.23723) audits poisoned memory post hoc by causal attribution; forensic trajectory signatures (arXiv:2606.30566), Bayesian trust scoring (arXiv:2603.02240) and provenance gating (arXiv:2608.10509) defend against adversarial injection; collective false memories (arXiv:2602.00428) leave the introducer's capability gap untested; 2605.22842 shows memory-layer misconduct is misattributed to model failure. None plants natural, non-adversarial failures by writer identity or measures the reader's own recall against a foreign judge's. In the home literature of self-training, confirmation bias in pseudo-labeling is countered by a second model's disagreement or ensemble diversity (arXiv:2310.14814, arXiv:2403.03095 cross pseudo-labeling), which is the parametric analog of the cross-judge arm. The archived idea lineage_blast_radius (4.75) was judged entailed by its consolidation rule; this design has no consolidation rule, plants contamination at controlled rates against a positive control, and measures precision/recall.
Abstract: Population and cross-model memory stores mix experience from many writers, and the literature asserts rather than measures whether a writer's errors propagate to a reader and whether the reader can tell. We manufacture contamination with writer identity as the manipulated variable. Base bank: the expert walkthrough pool for reader Qwen3-32B (clean gain +27/+32, Measurement A), with the reader's own matched-cost pool as a second base. Contaminants: failed training trajectories relabelled as successes (terminal failure line removed, a success line appended; selected for coherence, at most two 'Nothing happens' steps) from four writers: the reader's own policy (Q-self failures, on disk), the same backbone under a different temperature/scaffold at the same k=0 success (Q-prox; proximity varied at fixed capability), EXAONE-4.0-32B and gpt-oss-120b (different backbone; capability measured), plus a manufactured wrong-procedure graft on expert items (heat steps replaced by cool steps, success line kept) as the writer-agnostic positive control. Contaminants replace clean items per type at rates 0, 12.5, 25 and 50 percent at matched item count, with a length-matched clean placebo at 50 percent. The estimands are the retained fraction of the clean gain at each rate, rho_c(W, rate) = [S(contaminated) - S(static)] / [S(clean) - S(static)], the harm slope per writer, and read-time detection precision and recall when the reader (memory-free) is asked whether each retrieved item completes its stated task, scored per writer at matched item length, in a full judge x writer table (Q and E judging Q-self, Q-prox, E-self and G-self failures). Gate 0 requires the graft to cost >= 6 net points at 50 percent. The result would make writer identity, not just content, a required field for any read-time filter, and would identify the reader's own past failures as the worst-case contaminant in a shared store.
Experiments: Reader Q = Qwen3-32B primary; E = EXAONE-4.0-32B as second reader and as cross-judge (Gate V: serves in vLLM 0.13 and k=0 >= 0.30); G = gpt-oss-120b as writer and third judge if it serves. Failure pools: Q-self failures on disk (1,661 of 3,553 training games); Q-prox, E-self and G-self collected on the same 3,553 games (the successes serve the matrix design if run in the same program; here 8-14 GPU-hours on GPU1 while GPU0 evaluates). Masked contaminants: failures truncated at the last coherent action, terminal failure line removed, success line appended; coherence filter (<= 2 'Nothing happens', >= 1 correct object interaction); length reported per writer and matched across writers by selection. Contamination: per type, a fraction r of bank items replaced by contaminants of one writer at r in {0.125, 0.25, 0.5}; retrieval unchanged (task-description embedding, k=3; k=1 arm at 50 percent for Q-self). Cells for reader Q: 4 writers x 3 rates = 12; graft at 25 and 50 = 2; length-matched clean placebo at 50 = 1; clean base (rate 0) = 1; k=1 at 50 for Q-self and E-self = 2; self-pool base at 50 for Q-self and E-self = 2; two filter cells at 25 (own-judgment filter, cross-judge filter) = 2; static procedure and k=0 = 2: 24 cells x 548 episodes, 4 seeds for the 50 percent cells of Q-self, Q-prox, E-self and G-self (+4 cell-equivalents) = about 15,000 episodes; reader E cross-check at 50 percent for Q-self and E-self (2 cells) = 1,100 episodes. Analysis: harm slope per writer by paired linear fit over rates; rho_c per cell; recall/precision with Wilson intervals; the diagonal-deficit test is the interaction term judge x writer, not a main effect, so a uniformly better judge does not confirm the hypothesis. Total about 1.5 days on two A100s plus pool collections. Pre-registration of Gate 0, margins, coherence filter and cell list before the first confirmatory cell.
